title: Smoky Barbecue Plant-Based Burgers
subtitle: with Sweet Potato Wedges
description: You may notice this recipe's back for a victory lap – that's because sometimes you can't beat a tried-and-true winner! Our Dinnerly home cooks loved this recipe, so here it is again for you to enjoy its easy cooking, big flavours and satisfying goodness.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Cut the unpeeled sweet potato into wedges. Thinly slice the onion. Peel the cucumber into ribbons with a vegetable peeler. Put the cucumber and a pinch of salt in a bowl and toss to coat.

Roast sweet potato: Put the sweet potato on the lined tray. Scatter over the curry powder (see Make it yours), drizzle with 1 tbs olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Roast, turning halfway, for 20-25 mins until tender and golden.

Cook patties: While the sweet potato is cooking, put the plant-based mince and barbecue seasoning in a bowl. Using damp hands, combine well, than shape into 2 equal patties, slightly larger than the base of a bun. Heat 2 tsp olive oil in a medium frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the patties for 3 mins each side or until browned and cooked through. Remove from pan, reserving the oil in the pan.

Caramelise onion: Heat the reserved oil over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring, for 4 mins or until softened. Add 2 tsp balsamic vinegar, 2 tsp sugar and 60ml (¼ cup) water, season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 mins or until the onion is caramelised. Remove the pan from the heat.

Serve up: Meanwhile, cut the buns in half. Put on an oven tray, cut-side up, and bake for 5 mins or until toasted and golden. Spread the bun bases and tops with the mayonnaise and tomato sauce, if using. Layer the bases with the patties, cucumber ribbons and caramelised onion. Sandwich with the bun tops and serve with the sweet potato wedges. Enjoy!
Make it yours: Our curry powder is mild, but if you have little ones who aren't keen on too much spice, use less or don't sprinkle it over their portion of the wedges.
